title: Strong SetDisjointness conjecture
formal: Is it true that every static word-RAM data structure for SetDisjointness with space \(S(N)\) and worst-case query time \(T(N)\) satisfies \(S(N)T(N)^2=\widetilde\Omega(N^2)\)? The input is a list of nonempty sets \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\subseteq[N]\) with total size \(N=\sum_i|S_i|\), and a query \((i,j)\) asks whether \(S_i\cap S_j\) is empty.
definitions: A uniform sequential word RAM has a fixed finite program, word-sized registers and addressed memory cells. Unit-cost instructions are reads and writes, comparisons, branching, addition, subtraction, multiplication, integer division with nonzero divisor, Boolean bit operations and logical shifts. Arithmetic stored in one word is modulo \(2^w\); shifts by at least \(w\) yield zero. Addresses must fit the available word size. All table construction and input-dependent auxiliary memory count; there is no free advice or input-dependent oracle. Randomized programs may generate independent uniform random words. The sets are supplied as lists without repeated elements within a set, with \(m\le N\) and \(N\ge2\). Word size is \(w=\lceil10\log_2(N+2)\rceil\). Restrict attention to \(N\le S(N)\le N^2\), rounding up and padding unused cells if needed. Preprocessing may use arbitrary finite time; all input-dependent information retained afterwards counts toward \(S(N)\). A query reads this static representation and begins without input-dependent private state. Randomized preprocessing and query algorithms are allowed; the answer to each fixed input/query must be correct with probability at least \(2/3\). Space and query time bounds hold for every random outcome. The notation means that, for each admissible data structure, there are constants \(c>0\), \(b\ge0\), and \(N_0\) such that \(S(N)T(N)^2\ge cN^2/(\log(2+N))^b\) for all \(N\ge N_0\). All sizes are measured in words and time in word-RAM steps. Uniform programs and exact empty/nonempty semantics are required; reporting the intersection is another problem.
why: This conjecture underlies many space-query conditional lower bounds for text indexes, graph oracles and set systems.

context_blocks.text: The source proposes \(S=\widetilde\Omega(N^2/T^2)\) and describes a matching upper tradeoff. Preprocessing time and representation size are distinct resources here.
The conjecture concerns intersections of two already stored sets. The related multiphase problem instead receives an additional set after preprocessing.

notes: Uses an explicit bounded-error word-RAM convention for the source’s space-hardness conjecture. Relabeling the union of the sets into [N] preserves intersections and does not impose a restrictive universe promise.

sentences: A family of sets is stored in advance.
A query selects two stored sets and asks whether they intersect.
The conjecture relates the representation size to the square of query time.
Matching upper tradeoffs are known, but the general lower bound is not.
The target counts storage after preprocessing rather than the time spent preprocessing.
